title: Introduce zonal restore playbooks and in-place schema patcher
author: Elena Park
release_notes: Add zonal restore playbooks to reduce upgrade blast radius; introduce an in-place schema patcher that performs online compatibility checks and emits downgrade-blocker reports. Includes Helm/Terraform pinning and a new 'rpi migrate' preflight command.
description:
Context: On large on-prem clusters customers asked for safer, lower-blast-radius restores and a way to apply schema patches without full cluster downtime. This change adds two complementary features: (1) zonal restore playbooks that allow node-by-node/zone-by-zone restore sequencing and (2) an in-place schema patcher that validates forward/backward compatibility and can auto-generate a downgrade-blocker when a reverse migration is unsafe.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new 'rpi migrate preflight' command that runs offline schema checks, sample data verification, and a compatibility matrix against the running release manifest.
- Adds an 'rpi migrate apply --staged' flow that coordinates schema patch application zone-by-zone and emits a machine-readable runbook with step IDs and idempotency tokens.
- Introduces zonal restore playbooks under installer/playbooks/zonal-restore/* that contain Helm hooks, terraform scaling hints, and step templates for storage snapshot restoration per AZ.
- Adds a small Go library (installer/pkg/migrations/patcher) implementing an in-place SQL JSON-schema patcher that can perform forward/backwards inference and generate a 'downgrade-blocker' report.
- Pins several Terraform module versions and updates Helm charts to expose the new migration hooks (values.migration.enabled).

Safety model and rollback:
- By default the new CLI is opt-in; existing upgrades are unaffected.
- The preflight stage will block an apply if cross-node compatibility cannot be guaranteed; it produces a human-friendly and machine-readable report.
- The staged apply performs per-zone canaries: if a canary step fails, the runbook contains a deterministic rollback sequence to rehydrate the original snapshot for that zone and revert schema changes applied in subsequent steps.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for patcher logic (conservative compatibility heuristics).
- Integration CI job that runs a 3-zone full upgrade simulation using test fixtures and verifies runbook idempotency and rollback restore. The CI initially failed on a flaky restore timeout; the timeout was increased and the job stabilized.
- Manual verification on an internal lab cluster: performed a zonal restore with mixed-version replica set and demonstrated zero service-wide outage when following the playbook.

Why this is different from prior work: Several earlier PRs added snapshotting, rollbacks, and migration previews. This PR focuses on minimizing blast radius by shifting the restore/apply unit from cluster->zone and by providing an in-place schema patcher that explicitly reasons about downgrade safety and can halt the upgrade early with a clear remediation path.

Migration path for operators:
1) Install the updated Helm chart with values.migration.enabled=true in a staging cluster.
2) Run 'rpi migrate preflight --manifest=release.yaml --sample-set=smoke' and review the produced compat-report.json.
3) If preflight passes, run 'rpi migrate apply --staged --zones=zone-a,zone-b,zone-c --runbook-out=rb.json'. Follow the runbook step-by-step.

References: ENG-3412 (migration safety roadmap), SUP-1122 (customer report: restore blast radius), charts/CHANGELOG and terraform/modules/README for pinned versions.

review_comments:
Marco Silva: This looks good overall - can you clarify how the runbook ensures idempotency if an operator reruns a step?
Elena Park: The runbook includes step IDs and idempotency tokens; apply checks the token before executing and will no-op when it detects a completed step. Added tests to verify this.

Priya Desai: The compatibility heuristics are conservative; will this block benign changes (e.g., adding nullable columns)?
Elena Park: We treat nullable adds as forward/backward compatible. The heuristics are in patcher/heuristics.go and there's an escape hatch (--force) documented for emergency ops. I added more unit tests to cover these cases.

Oliver Chen: CI restore failed initially - was this addressed?
Elena Park: The integration job timed out on restore due to slow snapshot provisioning in the lab. Increased the timeout and added retry/backoff for snapshot attach. CI now passes.
